language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hi, I'm Chip.
Hi, my name is Johnny. I am here at my Grandma’s Italian restaurant. I am so excited to help her make my favourite lunch for her customers today ... pepperoni pizza!
Grandma says that we can’t start cooking until 11 ‘o clock. But how can we tell the time?
Take a look at the clock on our wall. See the short hand. It is also called the hour hand.
It goes from one number to the next in a clockwise rotation. It takes a whole hour for that to happen.
See the long hand? It is also called the minute hand. It also goes around the clock in a clockwise rotation, but for the minute hand, it goes all the way around the clock each hour.
Every hour, when the long hand is pointing to twelve and the short hand is pointing to a number it is an o’clock time.
So, if the long hand is pointing to twelve and the short hand is pointing to 7, it is seven o’clock.
Now the long hand is pointing to the twelve and the short one is pointing to the 11. This means it's 11 o'clock.
Time to start preparing the pepperoni pizza!
